fact: Statutory Instrument No. 67 of 2024, made by the Minister of Internal Affairs under section 85 of the Registration of Persons Act, Cap. 332, amends the Registration of Persons Regulations, 2015, showing the Act is in force as an Act of Parliament with regulations under it.

The Registration of Persons (Amendment) Regulations, 2024 (S.I. No. 67 of 2024), made 12 August 2024 under the Act, amend regulation 19 of the Registration of Persons Regulations, 2015 so a national identification card is valid for eleven years, deemed in force from 20 November 2015.

The Registration of Persons Act, 2015 (Chapter 332), an Act of Parliament assented to 26 March 2015, commenced that day for most Parts and on 1 January 2016 for Parts V and VI; it sets up the National Identification and Registration Authority, the National Identification Register and national identification cards.

The Registration of Persons Act, 2015 gives the Authority the function of creating the National Identification Register and assigning a unique national identification number to every person registered, and defines identity data to include biometric information and fingerprints.

The Parliament of Uganda news release of 20 August 2026 states that under the Registration of Persons Act, 2015, NIRA is mandated to create and run the National Identification Register and issue national identification cards (an Act of Parliament).
New Vision reports a NIRA statement of 3 June 2026 that registration of foreign residents is carried out under the Registration of Persons Act, CAP 332 (an Act), which NIRA treats as in force.

The NIRA statement of 3 June 2026 says that under section 72 of the Registration of Persons Act, CAP 332, registered foreigners are allocated a unique identification number, with an alien identification card issued under section 73.

The Registration of Persons (Amendment) Act, 2024, assented 15 July 2024, amends the Registration of Persons Act, 2015 (Act 4 of 2015) to empower NIRA to administer five civil registration laws, and starts on a date the Minister appoints by statutory instrument.

The committee report says the Registration of Persons Act was enacted on 26 March 2015 to establish a national identification register and NIRA and to provide for national identification cards, and the 2024 amendment bill would amend it.

Bill No. 39 of 2024 proposes to amend section 5 of the Registration of Persons Act 2015 (Act 4 of 2015), the existing law setting out the functions of the National Identification and Registration Authority.
